questions.q: Why does Caldwell's Priority 1 SLA Definition for a Meridian outage run with no `cmn_schedule` attached, while Priority 2 runs against an "8-5 Weekdays" schedule?
options: Because a company-wide Meridian outage is urgent around the clock, while Priority 2 work should only count business hours toward its target
Because Priority 1 incidents are not actually tracked with an SLA at all
Because schedules can only be attached to Priority 2 and lower definitions
Because the schedule field is cosmetic and doesn't change the duration math
questions.explain: An SLA with no schedule runs 24/7, which fits a round-the-clock Priority 1 commitment; an attached schedule makes the duration math business-hour-aware for lower priorities.

questions.q: Why does each SLA Definition's Start condition fire on State = In Progress rather than on record creation?
options: So queue time before an agent actually starts working the ticket doesn't get counted against the resolution target
Because In Progress is the only state ServiceNow allows a Start condition to reference
Because starting on creation would make the SLA breach immediately
Because Start conditions cannot reference the State field at all
questions.explain: Starting the clock on creation would bake in time the ticket simply sat unpicked, misrepresenting how fast the team actually worked once they started.

questions.q: Why does Caldwell's New Hire IT Setup catalog item attach separate SLAs to each Requested Item instead of one SLA on the overall Request?
options: Because the laptop-provisioning team and the access-approval team work on genuinely different fulfillment timelines
Because sc_request records are not allowed to have an SLA under any circumstances
Because attaching an SLA to sc_req_item is technically impossible
Because both items always finish at exactly the same time regardless of team
questions.explain: One SLA on the Request would force both items onto whichever timeline is slower, which is exactly the failure mode Chapter 4 warned about.

questions.q: What does the Request's own `request_state` show while the laptop item is Closed Complete but the access item is still Work in Progress?
options: A calculated Partially Complete status, rolled up from the combined state of its Requested Items
Closed Complete, because at least one item finished
A blank field, since the Request can't reflect mixed item states
Canceled, because the items are out of sync
questions.explain: A well-implemented rollup reflects honest mixed status instead of closing early the moment any one item finishes.

questions.q: Why does the article about the Line 3 printer's old intermittent-disconnect symptom get flagged for retirement once the failing switch is replaced?
options: So the Knowledge Base doesn't keep surfacing advice for a problem that no longer exists
Because Knowledge articles must be deleted automatically after 90 days
Because the article was never approved through the Draft-to-Publication workflow
Because retired articles are required before any new Problem can be opened
questions.explain: Retirement keeps the Knowledge Base trustworthy — an article describing a now-fixed issue would otherwise mislead the next agent who searches for that symptom.
